question: Which native MLP channels and layer updates are active at particular task and response tokens, and which observations predict a reproducible causal effect under direct edits?
parent_evidence: Existing post-gating capture and archived native profiles cover all 337920 MLP channels. They contain aggregate RMS and influence scores rather than a complete response timeline. Large activity alone has not established a semantic role or coding gain.
planned_observations: Read-only down_proj-input hooks measure actual post-gating channel values at fixed prompt positions and native cached response steps.
Keep signs, layer RMS/quantiles, compact top-magnitude channels, existing fixed candidates and raw output-column-norm summaries. Do not store full activation dumps.
Align activity with actual token IDs, source spans, predicted probabilities and independently recorded code behavior; include errors rather than only successful answers.
First validate that the observer preserves logits, emitted choices, cache, model state and hooks exactly on an actual random Gemma fixture.

Use the adequate-output baseline and unchanged donor records as possible own-trajectory lineage after that study closes. No closed completion or scorer is rerun. A new protocol must fix all cases and boundaries before model measurement.
Any neuron or transplant candidate requires a separately frozen zeroing, donor/self, rescue and matched-control test. Separate development selection from fresh utility confirmation.
not_permitted: Training, fitted strengths, vectors, alignments or a learned bridge
Semantic labels inferred from high activation alone
Cherry-picked tasks, response tokens or dramatic examples
A complete neuron map or novel general-method claim
next: Freeze the smallest informative observation protocol after the current source and baseline studies close; do not duplicate the active job.
